feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/analytics depth. It reads professionally, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited quantified outcomes beyond traffic/platform scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, culminating in leadership and then consulting; this strengthens credibility and seniority.  
- Strong domain alignment: web modernization, governance, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are consistently reinforced.  
- Good use of scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which adds impact and specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to create a tighter structure and avoid keyword overload.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: efficiency gains, engagement improvements, adoption rates, campaign results, cost savings, or team/budget size.  
- Fix stylistic consistency issues: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” vs. other hyphenation choices, and list punctuation (e.g., “web, email, social, and multimedia” uses a serial comma while some other lists do not). No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and experience. Tightening it and foregrounding the most distinctive value will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind” with a cleaner, more direct phrase like “leading enterprise platforms, governance, and content operations for.”
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent experience to increase credibility, e.g. “10,000+ page websites” or “high-volume member communications.”
- Consider trimming “multimedia production” here unless it’s central to target roles; the intro should prioritize enterprise web, governance, analytics, and AI.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading enterprise web platforms, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Drives website modernization, editorial systems, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- “Enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems” is echoed heavily in Topline Skills and Work Experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this section overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and with tighter, more parallel wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use concise, parallel noun phrases and reduce filler words like “operations” where possible.
- Emphasize the most senior/recent strengths first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, automation.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial systems • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestreaming
- Standardize style: use “web” instead of “website” for consistency with the rest of the CV; replace “&” with “and” if you want a more formal tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled…,” and governance/editorial systems repeat the header almost verbatim.
- Several items also duplicate Topline Skills; this section should stay high-level while Topline/Technical sections carry the detail.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the block is dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening wording and adding clearer outcomes or scope will make it feel more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short intro line like “Selected recent projects” and format each item consistently: project name + action + result/purpose.
- Tighten phrasing: “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” is strong; cut filler like “designed for continued campaign growth.”
- Where possible, add one concrete signal of scale, audience, or business value (for example, legislative content discovery, campaign engagement, conference activation).
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for cleaner CV prose.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current NACo role bullets; this block should emphasize standout examples, not restate responsibilities.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item here; consider leading with it to reduce repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads a bit generic and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries. Make it more consultative, outcome-oriented, and focused on what is new since returning as a consultant.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and enterprise web modernization for member-facing communications.”
- Replace task-heavy phrasing with impact verbs: “Designed and implemented…” / “Established workflows and analytics…” / “Led AI-enabled search initiative…”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4–5 bullets; combine CMS/front-end/troubleshooting into one execution bullet.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, toolkit downloads, publishing efficiency gains, search relevance improvements, stakeholder groups served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, and enterprise web improvement” repeats themes already covered in the Director of Digital Media role; emphasize advisory/consulting scope and new initiatives instead.
- Microsites and AI search also appear in Recent Projects, so keep this entry higher-level and reserve project specifics for that section.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s channel-management details.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Directed enterprise digital strategy, platforms, analytics, governance, and budget for NACo’s web, email, social, and video ecosystem.”
- Combine the website bullets and lead with the biggest achievement: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add % improvements for reporting speed, publishing efficiency, production cost savings, engagement, or turnaround time from the studio/analytics/governance work.
- Trim generic phrasing like “core digital communications channels” and “improving strategic decision-making”; replace with concrete operational results and leadership verbs such as modernized, scaled, standardized, launched.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed email newsletters/social media/video” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, modernization, and infrastructure.
- Video-programming language may duplicate the footer projects; mention the studio build here, not recurring series details.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good channel breadth, but the item reads generic and overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier digital/media role. Tighten it around execution, team coordination, and channel growth outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + function: “Ran day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and organization-wide editorial execution.”
- Replace “helping” phrasing with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Combine video/editorial workflow points into sharper impact language: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add a measurable or operational outcome if available: e.g., newsletter growth, send volume, video cadence/views, faster publishing, or number of cross-functional teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Improved workflows” and “strengthened editorial planning” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullets; keep this version focused on execution rather than enterprise leadership.
- Video-series language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; emphasize scaling/regularizing the program here, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing enterprise leadership and governance rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with tighter, less overlapping language:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience and stakeholder content strategy
- Consider swapping “messaging” for “communications” to sound more strategic and less tactical.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is vague; “Audience and stakeholder content strategy” better reflects senior ownership.
- If space allows, use separators instead of bullets for faster scanning in a skills section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems,” and “multi-channel communications” already appear in the header/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact same wording across all three sections.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Advocacy and public-sector communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Remove lower-priority or older-sounding items like jQuery unless it is still central to current work.
- Replace “Power Pages” and “SharePoint” with broader phrasing only if they are not important differentiators for target roles; keep Drupal first.
- If possible, add scale/context elsewhere on the CV rather than here, since the work history already proves impact (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid repeating the same platform list in both places.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in the header/core competencies, so keep wording concise here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics leadership and business impact over repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding • Web performance and SEO analysis • User behavior insights • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Put the most senior/value-add items first: KPI design, executive/leadership reporting, optimization insights.
- Tighten phrasing: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive dashboarding and reporting” and “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO and web performance optimization.”
- If accurate, add one higher-level term such as “analytics infrastructure” or “measurement strategy” to align with recent Director/Consultant work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills strategic and leave the full tool stack there.
- Avoid overemphasizing individual tools already named in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multiple NACo bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and tool/capability-led rather than a list of basic tasks.

Suggested edit
- Reframe to emphasize leadership and delivery scope: “Broadcast & Event Production” or “Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery.”
- Tighten and elevate the bullets to: “Video production & post-production • Livestream and webcast production • PTZ camera and studio systems • Hybrid, virtual and on-site event delivery”
- If accurate, add one stronger capability instead of a generic term: “Run-of-show design,” “technical direction,” or “speaker/remote contributor workflows.”
- Keep only 4 bullets max and avoid software/tool names here since those already appear in Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Livestreaming” duplicates “livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- “Studio operations” and video production are already supported by recent NACo experience; don’t overstate older production work here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should be tighter and emphasize strongest/recent platforms first.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine if Drupal is the clear lead; consider bolding or labeling Drupal as primary.
- Add light proficiency framing to increase signal, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector web modernization), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**.
- If space allows, group by use case for clarity: **Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint • Lightweight publishing: Power Pages, GitHub Pages**.
- Keep this item platform-only; save implementation detail for the coding/technical section.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider trimming one section or using this item for platforms only and the topline section for broader capabilities.
- “CMS modernization” and “AI-enabled search experiences” belong elsewhere, not in this platform list.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools that support recent delivery work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something like: “Front-End & Implementation Tools”
- Tighten and modernize the list: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Drop “jQuery” unless it is still actively used in current projects; if kept, place last or label as legacy support
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented qualifier tied to recent work, e.g., “used for Drupal front-end delivery, tagging, lightweight automation and deployment workflows”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same stack in both places
- “API integrations” and workflow-related tooling also overlap with “Automation & Workflow Systems,” so keep this item strictly implementation-focused

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools.”
- Group by function for faster scanning: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- Keep only tools you’ve used recently or at meaningful depth; if Trello/Basecamp were lighter-use, cut them to tighten the list.
- If space allows, add one short qualifier tied to impact: “Used to build editorial planning, approvals, and cross-team communications workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; include only if they support the workflow/operations story.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory rather than evidence of capability. Since recent roles already emphasize email operations, this item should stay concise and signal enterprise-level CRM/email systems rather than repeat newsletter work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email, CRM & Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely strategic weight/recency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of more tools: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation) • Higher Logic (member email/community communications) • Mailchimp**
- Keep formatting parallel with other technical items; avoid slashes if possible for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights and Journeys**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about newsletters and digital channels; don’t add outcome claims here unless they are removed elsewhere.
- “Engagement” may partially overlap with “Automation & Workflow Systems”; keep this item focused on email/CRM platforms only.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the NACo work bullets. Tighten it to emphasize methods and business use, not just a second list of platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Testing & Reporting**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI reporting • dashboard development • SEO analysis • experimentation/A/B testing**
- Put the strongest, most current tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.
- Replace vague “Dashboarding” with stronger phrasing like **dashboard development** or **executive reporting**; use **experimentation** if A/B testing was strategic rather than tool-specific.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly repeats the “Topline Skills” entry “Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one or making this section purely tool-based.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 NACo role, so avoid overstating them here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the 2018–2022 role on workflows, weekly video updates, and cross-channel operations. Make it more execution-focused and tie it to “firsts” or scale.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize concrete contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped build NACo’s first in-house digital team, establishing production workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital programming, including livestreams and weekly video updates for member and advocacy communications.”
- Tighten the management point: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” instead of “guidance.”
- If possible, add metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social reach, or efficiency gains from new workflows.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” is already covered in the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as the launch/build phase.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social” overlaps with later entries; avoid repeating the same operations language.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize coordination scope and the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Cut vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a clearer action, e.g., “produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications.”
- If possible, add scale or output: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, internal stakeholders served, or audiences reached.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so the progression feels upward and recent leadership remains dominant.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/multimedia bullets; avoid repeating broad production language.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here since stronger web/email/video ownership appears in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mixed capability list than a tight tools section. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills, so this entry should stay software/tool-focused and avoid repeating production functions.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast recording/editing • Livestream production systems”
- Standardize naming: use full Adobe product names for polish and consistency.
- Replace “Livestream studio workflows” with “Livestream production systems” or specific platforms/tools if available; “workflows” is vague.
